source.title: RAS-Eval: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Security Evaluation of LLM Agents in Real-World Environments
source.authors: Yuchuan Fu; Xiaohan Yuan; Dongxia Wang

record.file_problem: The text is mostly readable, but some content in Figures 6–8 is garbled. The relevant scaling-law discussion and Figure 4/Table 7 results are present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether performance increases with model scale using benchmark task scores and a fitted curve, rather than testing held-out pretraining loss or compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: The study reports a fitted relationship between Qwen-series model scale and security-benchmark performance scores. It does not report results on held-out pretraining loss, training tokens or compute, compute-optimal parameter/token allocation, architecture shape, other modalities, or general downstream tasks beyond this security benchmark.
record.test_reason: The study fits benchmark performance score against log parameter count for four Qwen models on its agent tool-use test tasks. This is a new downstream setting with a result on whether performance rises with scale (V6). It does not measure pretraining loss, tokens, compute or allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors say the Figure 4 fit shows larger Qwen models score higher, 'aligning with the scaling laws'. They use this as evidence that the benchmark discriminates between models. However, the fitted score is benign-task tool-call performance over 4 Qwen models, not security under attack. The abstract's 'scaling laws held for security capabilities' overstates what was measured.
record.recipe_differences: The study relates security-benchmark task scores to model scale using a fitted curve; it does not use held-out pretraining loss or sweep training tokens and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The text reports score variation between Qwen models at identical parameter scales and a confidence interval that widens at larger scales.
record.problems: The scaling result is based on Qwen-series security-benchmark scores, not pretraining loss. The text reports variation at identical parameter scales and a widening confidence interval; numerical individual scores and interval values are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported scaling results left out.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation of fits from small runs to much larger runs.
Effects of depth, width or shape at fixed parameter count.

Relation of downstream performance to pretraining loss; predictive extrapolation to unseen scales; model families other than Qwen; scaling of attack robustness, since attack tasks were run only on GLM4-Flash.
Dependence of exponents or fits on setup or fitting choices; curve bending.

missing.what: Per-model human–model Kappa agreement for Qwen models, which rises with size: 1.5B 0.4312, 7B 0.6838, Plus 0.7468, Max 0.7847. GLM4-Flash (0.6708) and Llama3.2-3B (0.5823) are also reported.
Per-model score, TCR and TIR across all six models, shown in a figure only with no numbers in the text.

record.verdict_notes: Study is a security benchmark paper; the scaling check is a benchmark-validity sanity test. The tranche was changed from T2 to T3 because this is a new downstream setting, not a different method aimed at loss scaling. The record's limits_scope label is dropped. A widening confidence interval reflects fit uncertainty, not a qualification of V6. R2 cannot be assessed because Qwen-Plus and Qwen-Max sizes are undisclosed. The abstract says 6 models, Section 3.1.1 says eight, and the conclusion says 7. Figure 4's y-axis spans roughly 30–130, although Eq. 5–6 scores lie in [0,1]; the scale is unexplained.

rows.subject: Qwen-series models (aggregate fitted curve)
rows.size_stated: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen-Plus, and Qwen-Max; parameter counts are not stated for all models
rows.stage_stated: instruct for the two Qwen2.5 models; not stated for Qwen-Plus and Qwen-Max
rows.operation_detail: Fit a curve relating Qwen-series model parameter count to security-benchmark performance score.
rows.measure: Performance score versus logarithmic parameter count; reported fit statistics
rows.value: The text reports an overall upward trend as logarithmic parameter count increases. Table 7 reports SSE 68.0004, R2 0.9051, adj_R2 0.8577, and RMSE 5.8310.
rows.uncertainty: A 95% confidence interval is shown; the text says it widens at larger scales. Numerical interval values are not stated.
rows.note: The curve and its trend are shown in Figure 4; the fit statistics are given in Table 7. The authors describe the fit as strong and say larger models generally achieve higher scores.
rows.check: Subject and measure need restating. The 'performance score' (Eq. 5–6) measures correct tool calls on benign test tasks, not security under attack. The fit covers only 4 models: the adj_R2 of 0.8577 implies n=4 with one predictor. The x-axis label is 'ln(ln(B))', and Qwen-Plus and Qwen-Max have undisclosed parameter counts, so their x-positions are unverifiable. Baseline is not applicable.

rows.subject: Qwen-Plus and Qwen-Max
rows.size_stated: The text says the compared models have identical parameter scales; exact parameter counts are not stated.
rows.operation_detail: Compare performance scores at identical parameter scales.
rows.value: The text states that scores vary at identical parameter scales and that Qwen-Max and Qwen-Plus achieve relatively higher scores at certain scales; numerical values are figure only.
rows.note: The text explicitly describes score variation among models at identical parameter scales, but does not give the underlying numerical scores.
rows.check: Qwen-Plus and Qwen-Max parameter counts are not disclosed, so 'identical parameter scales' cannot be checked. No numeric scores are given, and the text does not show these models deviating from the fitted trend. This should not be marked partial.

relationships.condition: Four Qwen-series models on RAS-Eval benign test tasks (tool-call performance score)
relationships.reason: Score rises with log parameter count, with fitted R2 0.9051 (R1). Evidence is weak: only 4 points, and two models have undisclosed sizes.
relationships.display_finding: Tool-call scores increased with log parameter size with fitted R² of 0.9051 across four models, although two model sizes were undisclosed.
